Operating Characteristics of the gBOIN Design

Source: R/sim_gboin.R
sim_gboin.Rd

Simulate trials of the gBOIN design of Mu et al. (2019) for a toxicity outcome with several grades that each carry a score, and summarize how often each dose is selected as the MTD and how the patients are distributed over the doses.

Usage

sim_gboin(
  target,
  p_grade,
  score,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = 18,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  elim_rule = c("posterior", "count"),
  min_mtd_sample = 1,
  overdose_cutoff = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.313 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5. See the details.

p_grade

Numeric matrix. True probability of each toxicity category (rows, from the lowest to the highest) at each dose (columns, in increasing dose order). Every column sums to 1.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at the current dose and the design would stay there. Defaults to 18. A value above the maximum sample size switches the rule off.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest mean score deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest mean score deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for dose elimination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

elim_rule

Character scalar, either "posterior" or "count". How a dose is eliminated. Under "posterior", the default and the rule of the article, the posterior probability is evaluated at the total score. Under "count" the dose is eliminated when the total score reaches the elimination boundary of the number of DLTs of boin_boundary, a whole number, as in the 'UnifiedDoseFinding' package. See the details.

min_mtd_sample

Integer scalar. Smallest number of patients a dose must have been given to be selected as the MTD. Defaults to 1.

overdose_cutoff

Numeric scalar or NULL. Doses with a true mean normalized score above this value count as overdoses in the summary. Defaults to NULL, the target.

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar, either "with_stay" or "simple". Under "with_stay" the trial stops at n_earlystop only when the design would remain at the current dose. Under "simple" it stops as soon as the threshold is reached.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the trial level data in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report the progress in messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class c("gboin_oc", "boin_oc"), a list with the components of the result of sim_boin, in which

p_true

is the true mean normalized score of each dose,

n_tox_dose, total_n_tox

are averages of the total normalized score, in the place of the number of DLTs,

and in addition

design

The name of the design, "gBOIN".

p_grade, score

The true grade probabilities and the scores.

n_grade_dose

Matrix, toxicity categories by doses, of the average number of patients in each category.

With keep_trials = TRUE the component trials also holds the array n_grade of gboin_simulate.

Details

The trials are simulated by gboin_simulate, which describes the design, and the MTD is selected by gboin_select_mtd. A trial stopped because the lowest dose is eliminated selects no dose.

With two toxicity categories of scores 0 and 1 the design is the BOIN design, and the result is, for the same seed, that of sim_boin without titration.

The result can be passed to oc_results and oc_compare, where it appears under the name gBOIN.

References

Mu, R., Yuan, Y., Xu, J., Mandrekar, S. J. and Yin, J. (2019). gBOIN: a unified model-assisted phase I trial design accounting for toxicity grades, and binary or continuous end points. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C, 68, 289-308. doi:10.1111/rssc.12263

See also

gboin_simulate, gboin_select_mtd, sim_gboin_multi, sim_boin

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Mu et al. (2019): grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4 at six doses,
# equivalent toxicity scores 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5, target score 0.47
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.83, 0.75, 0.62, 0.51, 0.34, 0.19),
  c(0.12, 0.15, 0.18, 0.19, 0.16, 0.11),
  c(0.04, 0.07, 0.11, 0.14, 0.15, 0.11),
  c(0.01, 0.03, 0.09, 0.16, 0.35, 0.59)
)
oc <- sim_gboin(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5,
  p_grade = p_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5),
  n_cohort = 10,
  cohort_size = 3,
  n_earlystop = 100,
  n_trials = 500,
  seed = 123
)
oc
#> gBOIN operating characteristics
#>   target score    : 0.3133333
#>   trials          : 500
#>   cohorts         : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size : 30
#>   lambda_e / _d   : 0.2471 / 0.3746
#> 
#>                  DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5  DL6 Total / No MTD
#> True score (%)   7.7 12.7 22.3 31.7 50.3 70.0               
#> MTD selected (%) 0.2  3.4 32.0 53.8 10.4  0.2            0.0
#> Patients treated 3.6  5.2  9.2  9.0  2.7  0.3           30.0
#> Toxicity score   0.3  0.6  2.0  2.9  1.4  0.2            7.5
#> 
#> Doses above a true score of 0.3133333: DL4, DL5, DL6

#>   Trials treating over 80% there      : 0%
